extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit organizations, community development financial institutions, and other partners seeking Kresge Foundation grants or social investments
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Kresge Foundation's grantmaking and social investment policies, priorities, geographic focus, and how it solicits proposals (invitations, LOIs, RFPs). Useful for organizations seeking funding or partnership with Kresge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and duration of grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Our programs work both independently and in collaboration to award single-year and multiyear grants that fund general operating, projects and planning activities advancing strategic objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants may support general operating expenses, discrete projects, or planning work. Programs may coordinate or operate independently when awarding these grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application solicitation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Most often, we invite applicants. Occasionally, program teams issue an open call for LOIs within a focus area. For initiatives, programs typically use an open request-for-proposals process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not assume open solicitations; check the Current Funding Opportunities page for any listed open opportunities. Prepare for invited applications, occasional LOI open calls, or formal RFP processes for initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of our funding is to work in the U.S. but our Education Program also supports a portfolio of institutions in South Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be primarily U.S.-based or working in U.S. contexts unless applying to the specific Education Program portfolio that includes South Africa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and annual funding priorities by program
rubrics_metrics.description: Annually, Kresge makes more than 400 grants to nonprofits. Our annual give has averaged around $160 million in recent years, always in accordance with IRS guidance to give at least 5% of our endowment on a five-year rolling basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-level funding totals (2024 example): American Cities $20.8M; Arts & Culture $15.6M; Detroit $26.4M; Education $23.8M; Environment $13.8M; Health $10.4M; Human Services $18.1M; Social Investment Practice $1.4M. Use these figures to gauge relative program emphasis and possible scale of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Investment practice purpose and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe in using multiple forms of capital to create change. The Social Investment Practice partners with programs to complement their efforts by unlocking capital streams with loans, deposits, equity and guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge combines grants and social investments to create more sustainable impact. Applicants or partners should consider blended-capital approaches (debt, equity, guarantees, deposits) where appropriate to program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Investment submission policy (no unsolicited proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Social Investment Practice does not accept unsolicited proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social investments are frequently funded through intermediaries such as Community Development Financial Institutions, and the Practice also makes direct investments in nonprofits. Prospective applicants should seek partnership routes (CDFIs, intermediaries) or await invitation; do not submit unsolicited proposals to the Social Investment Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for intermediaries and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: It frequently funds its work through intermediaries such as Community Development Financial Institutions but also makes direct investments in nonprofits. We frequently partner with the public and private sectors and other funders or investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge favors leveraging intermediaries (e.g., CDFIs) and cross-sector partnerships (public/private/funders) when making social investments; structuring proposals or partnerships to include such intermediaries may align with their approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level active social investment portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Social Investments — Active Portfolio (Sept. 2024) lists commitments by program (e.g., American Cities $35M; Detroit $39.2M; Arts & Culture $12.5M; Education $7.1M; Environment $52M; Health $28.5M; Human Services $12M; Social investment practice $42.6M; Marygrove $132M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The active portfolio numbers indicate where social investment capital is currently concentrated. Applicants and partners can infer priority areas and relative investment activity from these figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for funding city programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Why We Fund Programs for Cities: 'Cities Are Powerful Vehicles of Change'; 'Cities’ Density of Assets Can Contribute to Expanded Equity and Opportunity'; 'Cities Are Amenable to Philanthropic Engagement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge values city-focused work that leverages urban concentrations of activity and assets to drive innovation, scale equity-enhancing solutions, and engage cross-sector leadership. Proposals that demonstrate these characteristics are likely aligned with the foundation's rationale for funding cities.
